Is there life after death? Is communication with the deceased possible?
By what means does science attempt to achieve communication with the dead? – The disagreement between spiritualism and psychophysiology. – Interview with Mr. Angg. Tanagras

The question of the existence or not of a soul living even after the death of the human being, and above all of its communication with the living, occupies world science. As we saw in yesterday's beginning of this research, the studies and experiments have presented astonishing phenomena. In the explanation of these phenomena, however, world science is divided into two great camps: the spiritualists and the students of psychology.

The former are convinced that it concerns pure communication with the spirits of deceased humans. The latter, on the contrary, study the phenomena, experiment, and investigate without expressing a clear opinion as to whether they concern the spirits of the dead or other invisible supernatural forces.

There is also in Athens a Society for Psychophysiology, which investigates the phenomena produced by invisible and mysterious forces. Its experiments are exceptionally interesting and are explained in many ways. They nevertheless remain mysterious.
What Mr. A. Tanagras says

The president and director of the experiments and research of the Society for Psychophysiology of Athens is the former surgeon-general of our navy, Mr. Angelos Tanagras (Evangelidis). It was to him that we first turned to have his views on the most important and eternal question of metapsychic phenomena and the communication of the souls of the deceased with the living.
Mr. Tanagras received us most kindly, as always, at the Society's office. We communicated to him the questions of our research. And after thinking for a moment, he told us:

Science takes nothing as certain before investigation, but it also rules out nothing. In the present study of the question of life beyond death, we do not take it as certain before investigation that a soul exists and communicates with the living. Nor, however, do we rule out such an eventuality, if it is scientifically proven. Science sets no limits before investigation. It investigates, experiments, and reaches conclusions.

— But, we brought to Mr. Tanagras's attention, that very many societies for psychical research accept spiritualism and believe that the souls of the dead cause numerous phenomena and communicate with the living…

— Indeed. Those are the purely spiritualist societies. Psychophysiology, however, does not take communication with the dead as given. The spiritualists, as you know, developed their system from 1848. It was then that the phenomena of the Fox family occurred, in Hydesville, America.

The daughter of the family, who was evidently a medium, produced noises without touching the spot where they occurred. A kind of telekinesis. They then thought whether these noises might originate from the spirit of a deceased person. And they began to ask various questions, e.g. 'if this is so, knock once; if that, twice.'
Then gradually they also formed an alphabet with knocks. And the conversation of the living with the hypothetical spirits began.
How spiritualism developed

At that time science had not yet studied these phenomena and various hypotheses were formed. In the end, no other explanation could be given than that these knocks were made by the souls of the dead and that they, with the code alphabet, were answering the questions. Specifically for the case of the Fox girl, it was believed that the spirit of someone murdered in the house years previously was speaking.

From there, spiritualism began, which quickly gained wide currency in both America and England. Later in France, Professor Hippolyte Denizard appeared, who under the pseudonym Allan Kardec wrote a series of volumes on spiritualist research. Kardec's works are considered the Gospel of spiritualism.
In them he laid the foundations of the theory, explained on this basis the experiments, and guided those who wished to experiment and speak with their deceased…

From that time, spiritualist research has multiplied throughout the world. The whole globe is engaged in spiritualism. Tables move, mediums write to the dictation of spirits, etc. This movement also reached Athens and threw it into turmoil many years ago.
And all the spiritualists, full of mysticism, blindly believed that they were speaking with the souls of the dead. And they believe it to this day.
The newer research

But in 1882 another kind of research began. The first Society for Psychical Research was founded in London, and science began new research, coldly and without any mysticism or prejudice. And this research proved that there do indeed exist and operate forces beyond matter — immaterial and unknown psychic forces.
When I was studying, I too was a materialist. Büchner and Haeckel were my gospels. But later, especially after the discovery of radioactivity, I became convinced that immaterial forces also exist.

So I too turned to spiritualism. I saw that there is an immaterial world, superior forces. I have therefore been engaged since then with experiments. And I became convinced of the fact of the existence of invisible forces. But I was not convinced that the spirits of the dead produce these phenomena. And I will explain to you why.
— Let us hear your reasoning.

— Well, if it were possible, as the spiritualists claim, for the dead and the living to communicate, would there remain unsolved crimes? Would there be treasures hidden by the deceased and still unknown? Would there be lost wills and so many other things? Would the spirits of the dead not tell all to the living?
Besides, would there be unsolved problems in science, in physics, in chemistry? Would the great scientists who died before us not solve them?
Certainly we do not deny that spirits survive after death.
But they do not communicate with the living. At least up to the present, this has not been demonstrated.
TOMORROW: The astonishing phenomena.
Fotos Giofillis
ETHNIKI SIMAIA, 22.01.1935

content.value: Communication with the Dead – Spiritualism – Psychophysiology (1935) – Part 1
Is it possible to communicate with the deceased?
By what means does science attempt to achieve it
The astonishing scientific discoveries – Supernatural phenomena are confirmed – The activity of invisible forces – What spiritualism accepts and what psychophysiology accepts
By our distinguished man of letters and contributor, Mr. Fotos Giofillis
Is there life after death?
That is to say, does something of the human existence live on in the beyond?
If there is life after death, can we communicate and come to an understanding with those who have died?

These two great questions have tormented people of all times and places. They are the great questions which have always been topical. All wise men studied them, scientists researched them, writers and poets examined them… And around them has revolved and continues to revolve all of humanity's attention.

In these days, however, they are more topical than ever. Because science has been very seriously engaged in recent years with experiments and all manner of investigations to illuminate them, to give an answer to anxious humanity.
The two camps of researchers
Researchers are now divided into two camps. On one side there are the researchers of psychophysiology, and on the other the researchers of spiritualism.

The former investigate, study, experiment, without taking anything as certain. They do not accept the idea that the spirits of the dead communicate with us in any way. They do, however, examine the phenomena of psychophysiology and draw their own conclusions, based on the theory of the existence of invisible forces in the human body.

The spiritualists, on the contrary, accept the communication and mutual understanding of the spirits of the deceased with the living. They accept without question that the dead can come to an understanding with the living, and to this end they employ various means: the well-known table, writing, hypnosis, etc.

The disagreement, therefore, of the two great schools that investigate metapsychic phenomena is only theoretical. One accepts that the mysterious phenomena originate only from the deceased, and the other accepts that they originate only from the living.
There are also, however, researchers who divide the mysterious phenomena of our life into those originating from the souls of the dead and those created by mysterious influences of living persons.

Regardless of theories, however, all researchers together accept the mysterious phenomena as real. These are: the transmission of thoughts without external agency, that is, telepathy; the movement of objects without anyone touching them; prophetic predictions; mysterious coincidences; but also the mysterious force of the human body; the appearance of ghosts and of invisible forces that are materialised for a short time; as well as a host of other very strange phenomena.

Once we have it as a scientifically established fact that the phenomena exist, we return to the initial questions, but modified. That is: is there life after death? And do these phenomena originate from the living or from the dead who communicate with us? It is on these questions that world science is investigating and reflecting today.
The supernatural phenomena
Let us now see how the human being observed the supernatural phenomena, the mysterious psychic or spiritual events, and how he began to study them.

It is a fact that from very ancient times man had a tendency to observe and believe in the supernatural. He loves stories that contain supernatural phenomena and seeks to learn everything that is outside the laws of nature.

From earlier times there were traditions according to which many people saw 'house shadows', that is white or black ghosts that live in a house and knock mysteriously on the walls or overturn various objects.

Then they began to believe that the 'shadow' was a person who had been killed inside that house or who was passing by when the foundation stone of the house was being laid and died within the year, but whose soul remained for ever as a ghost inside the house.

From ancient times people have also believed that some individuals see 'shadows' and ghosts and others do not. Those who see them are called 'light-shadowed' (alafroïskiotoi) and those who do not see them are called 'heavy-shadowed' (varïskiotoi).
And modern tradition explains who became 'light-shadowed'. Who do you think? Those whose godfather happened to make a mistake when he said the 'Creed' at their baptism…
These and other stranger things does the people believe about the appearance of supernatural phenomena.
But the people also interpret dreams metaphysically. There are good dreams and bad. Prophetic dreams, but also insignificant dreams. All these the tradition and superstition presents and examines.

But science today believes, examines, and studies them too. The time has passed when science was atheistic and materialistic. Today it acknowledges, for the most part, the existence of invisible forces.

The first spiritualist phenomena that science studied occurred in America in 1848, that is 87 years ago. In Hydesville, a poor village in the United States of America, unusual knocks were often heard at night in a house.
The cause of these knocks was unknown and mysterious. No visible reason caused them. In this house lived the Fox family, who calmly began to examine the sounds.
It had no foolish fears or superstitions to make it frightened. But the knocks continued frequent and persistent.

Finally the Fox family noticed that these knocks occurred only when their daughter, Katie Fox, a girl of 12 years, was in the house. When she was away from the house, the mysterious knocks were never heard.
Then they noticed that the number of knocks was also regulated by Katie's will. She herself was amazed that it sufficed for her to think of a number of knocks in order to hear them on the wall.
She would call out that she wanted so many knocks to be heard, and immediately they were heard.
Then she gave the command by thought alone, without speaking at all, and again the knocks that the girl commanded occurred.

A crowd of people from all over the village ran every day to that house. Then curious onlookers, students, scientists, and scholars began to gather from the surrounding area and from all over America. And all remained astonished at this phenomenon.
Gradually specialist scientists tried to explain the event. And then they noticed that the unknown force making the knocks answered certain questions, though always with a certain number of knocks.
So they determined that the unknown force would knock once to say 'Yes' and twice to say 'No'.
Then the girl asked: 'Who are you? Are you perhaps a soul?'
One knock was heard. That is: 'Yes.'
'So you are a soul, the spirit of a deceased person?' This at least was what the specialist scientists accepted.
Then the dialogue continued in the same manner and it was established that the phenomenon was produced by an invisible thought.
The little girl was the intermediary, the 'medium', between the visible and the invisible world. And thus the experiments immediately began. In this way Spiritualism was born.
Spiritualism is the theory and all the experimental work that demonstrates that living people can communicate with the deceased.
The progress of spiritualism
Spiritualism advanced quickly. First in America, then in England and France, and afterwards throughout the civilised world.
Gradually many 'mediums' were found in all parts of the earth, from England to Australia. And the experiments were and continue to be conducted intensively everywhere.
Many specialist societies were formed and myriads of educated people, scientists, writers, and scholars occupied themselves with the study of spiritualist phenomena.

Astonishing experiments were conducted. They reached as far as the materialisation of spirits, that is, spirits took on a material form for a short time. And the experiments continue with astonishing results!
Nevertheless today, as we have seen, the psychical researchers who examine these phenomena are divided. And besides the spiritualists there are the followers of psychophysiology.
These do accept all the phenomena, but attribute them all to invisible and metaphysical forces of living people.

And here in Athens, where in other times, in the age of the poet G. Souris, spiritualist experiments had triumphant successes, and where later spiritualist societies were formed with learned researchers and experimenters, today there is the 'Society for Psychophysiology', which carries out most important experiments, but does not take as its theoretical basis the communication of the deceased with the living.
ETHNIKI SIMAIA, 21.01.1935
